# Outage-Proof Livestream

> A free, open-source Windows service that makes church livestreams
> outage-proof. OBS records the service to a local file on disk and never
> touches the network; a small pusher service tails that growing file and
> pushes it to a relay VPS, which fans it out to YouTube. Any network,
> router, or relay outage means zero content loss -- the disk file is the
> buffer, and the pusher resumes from the exact byte offset it left off at,
> catching up faster than realtime so the stream stays gap-free.

Licensed under the AGPL-3.0. Built by church members of LOGINGRUPA Ltd. at
Spirit and Truth city church, Lielvarde, Latvia.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/logingrupa/outage-proof-livestream): full source, issues, and releases
- [README](https://github.com/logingrupa/outage-proof-livestream/blob/main/README.md): architecture, requirements, and both quickstarts, in plain Markdown
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/logingrupa/outage-proof-livestream/blob/main/LICENSE): AGPL-3.0 licence text

## Page sections

- [The problem](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#problem): why a dropped connection normally means lost stream content
- [How it works](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#how-it-works): the disk-file-as-buffer architecture and byte-offset resume
- [Quickstart](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#quickstart): install steps for the church PC and the relay VPS
- [Transport choice](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#transport): tcp (default) vs srt (advanced), and why
- [Requirements](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#requirements): what the church PC and the relay VPS each need
- [FAQ](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#faq): common volunteer questions, answered
- [Mission](https://logingrupa.github.io/outage-proof-livestream/#mission): why this project exists and who built it
